name: UACE-9: Valid Command Flooding
description: An abnormally high volume of commands from one source in a short window — a command flood, whether a denial attempt or rapid attack automation.
query:
FROM logs.ecs.spacecraft.commands
| WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours AND source.ip IS NOT NULL
| STATS commands = COUNT(*) BY source.ip, window = BUCKET(@timestamp, 5 minute)
| WHERE commands > 8
| KEEP source.ip, window, commands
| LIMIT 100
author: Elastic
false_positives: An authorized operations script or planned command burst produces high volume. Tune the threshold and add exceptions per mission.

## SPARTA Investigation Guide

### Detection logic
An ES|QL aggregation over the command feed that counts commands per source per five-minute window and flags any source exceeding the routine rate, surfacing a command flood on the channel.

### Framework reference
- **Tactic:** Execution
- **Technique EX-0013:** [Flooding](https://sparta.aerospace.org/technique/EX-0013/)
- **Indicator of Behavior UACE-9:** An abnormally high rate of valid commands from one source.

### Indicators of Behavior
- **UACE-9: An abnormally high rate of valid commands from one source.**

### How to validate this alert
Review the source's command sequence for the window. A burst of destructive or repeated commands is high-confidence abuse; a burst of routine housekeeping may be a script. Correlate with the hazardous-command rule and ask the AI agent to attribute the source. See spartastixkb.
